articles.title: Cs Ivory Indigo
articles.summary: Grey-beige marbled base with soft lilac and pink swirls and speckles, muted and dreamy. Reads as a nearly solid plum-magenta with a faint sandy grain; the horizontal bars show as a few light and dark streaks across a panel.
articles.what: Up close: Magenta-purple field with a fine blotchy grain, 3-6 px, in two close tones of magenta and violet. A few glitch-like horizontal bars cut across it: dark purple strips, pale lilac blocks and thin light lines, 10-300 px long, like torn pixel rows from a bad scan. From a distance: Reads as a nearly solid plum-magenta with a faint sandy grain; the horizontal bars show as a few light and dark streaks across a panel. Measured spec (average): metal 102, roughness 72, coat 147. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, sides, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Cs Ivory Indigo" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: even colour and grain read on any panel
Hood and roof: soft metal glow shows
White, gold or silver numbers with an outline read well; purple and dark numbers vanish.
Bold stripes, numbers and graphics in white, gold or black: strong contrast on plum
Pairs well with: white, chrome, lilac, black.
pitfalls: Not a pure solid colour: a fine grain and a few torn horizontal bars show
Not a pattern: the bars are rare and look like a flaw, not a design
Avoid: small numbers over busy swirl, next to other patterned finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 102 (pearl-level metal), roughness 72 (satin gloss), clearcoat 147 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over busy swirl, next to other patterned finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold stripes, numbers and graphics in white, gold or black: strong contrast on plum; tribal, script or racing graphics: the grain does not fight clean shapes
Patterns to avoid: fine weaves, carbon, flake: noise on noise; other glitch or horizontal-stripe patterns: doubles the bars
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat spec: deepens the plum; none needed: base already has medium metal
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
